To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The incidence of duodenal leak is higher in patients undergoing a Billroth I procedure than in those who undergo a Roux‐en‐Y procedure; 2) Duodenal leak is more common in patients with a history of Billroth II procedure; and 3) Duodenal stump leak is a significant risk factor for postoperative mortality.
endoscopic clipping of a duodenal stump leak is a feasible and safe method of treatment.

1) the use of the endoscope in the treatment of duodenal leak is safe, effective and feasible; 2) the use of endoscopic clips in duodenal leakages is safe and effective; 3) endoscopic clips can be placed in a duodenal leak with no risk of perforation or bleeding; and 4) the use of clips to close a duodenal perforation can be used in the treatment of patients with a high surgical risk.
